title: Console bug cadence log — Noah personal scratch
body:
Goal: clear the small pile of console/dashboard bugs that customers flagged over the last 48h. This is a running scratchpad — quick notes, replication steps, mitigation, owners, and micro-decisions. Use this to triage, assign, and convert to formal tickets if needed.

TODAY (quick run):
- 09:10 sync with Maya (10m): handoff on INC-4821 and confirm repro steps from customer (Acme Retail).
- 10:00 run dashboard snapshot for acct: acme-retail-prod (time window: 2026-03-09 02:00 -> 2026-03-09 04:00) to check gap in token-cost metric.
- 11:30 quick smoke after rolling patch to widget-service (canary 10% -> 50%).

INC-4821 (customer: Acme Retail) — gap in token-cost per-route
- Symptom: token-cost graph drops to zero for ~7m at 02:37 UTC on 2026-03-09. Spike in 5xxs right after.
- Customer report: "our cost view shows zero tokens during a window; billing unaffected but UI blank".
- Quick hypothesis: metrics ingestion dropped for that tenant (ingest pipeline partition) OR dashboard query had date-shift bug.
- Quick checks performed: 
  * curl to metrics API: /v1/metrics/series?org=acme-retail&metric=token_cost&start=2026-03-09T02:00Z&end=2026-03-09T04:00Z -> returned empty series at 02:36-02:44.
  * Checked kafka consumer lag on metrics-ingest-prod-3: lag=0, but consumer restarted at 02:35 (kube event).
  * pod logs (metrics-ingest-prod-3): see stack trace "Partition assignment failed: timeout waiting for group coordinator" at 02:34.
- Immediate mitigation: restarted metrics-ingest-prod-3 (done 2026-03-09 03:05) -> rehydrated series backfill kicked off.
- Customer-facing note (to send): short explanation + status + ETA for backfill (1-2h depending on backfill size). Draft: "We observed a transient ingestion disruption tied to a consumer restart; data backfill is in progress and UI should reflect values within 2 hours. We're adding auto-restart guard and improved alerting."
- Next action: create tech-debt ticket to add restart guard + automated backfill trigger for partitions that lag > 5m. Owner: Maya. JIRA suggestion: ENG-td-metrics-backfill-#?.

BUG: dashboard tile not honoring time-range selection (internal)
- Repro: open Dashboard D-210 (team: Payments) -> set time range to last 15m -> tile "p95-latency" shows last 24h instead.
- Hypothesis: tile caches a pre-computed query when the dashboard sync job runs; new selector not propagated. Maybe LRU cache key uses dashboard_id only, not time_range param.
- Quick local repro steps: 
  * Open curl to dashboard API: GET /api/dashboard/D-210?time=last_15m -> payload includes time_range param but cache-key header X-Cache-Key shows outdated key.
  * Dev-mode request bypass cache (add header X-Cache-Bypass:true) returns expected 15m series.
- Temporary workaround: add UI toggle on team dashboards to force bypass for now (low UI effort, 30m).
- Longer fix: update cache key to include time_range hash. Dev owner: Luca. PR in progress: GH-PR-678.

Small annoyances / follow-ups
- Logging noise: repeated "metric decode failed" warnings from metric-serializer (trace id pattern mser-*) — root cause unknown. Add alert only if >100/min to avoid noise.
- Customer A (Parcelly) flagged an old bug where embeddings explorer times out on large files. They gave repro (uploads >250MB) -> create dedicated follow-up: scale upload timeout and surface progress bar. Owner: Aisha.
- Investigate whether recent KV cache warmups correlate with increased mempressure on route-worker-7. Check heap profiles from 2026-03-08 01:00UTC.

Notes to self: heuristics and quick commands
- grep logs quickly: kubectl logs -n prod metrics-ingest-prod-3 --since=6h | rg "Partition assignment failed|error"
- snapshot time series: python tools/ts_dump.py --org acme-retail --metric token_cost --start 2026-03-09T02:00Z --end 2026-03-09T05:00Z --out /tmp/acme-token-cost.json
- check kafka consumer status: kubectl exec -n prod kafka-consumer-ctl -- /bin/consumer-lag --group metrics-ingest --topic tokens-v2
- suggested slack msg to #console-alerts: "Heads up — transient metrics ingestion restart at 02:34 UTC affected a small set of orgs; backfill in progress. Tracking: INC-4821. Please escalate if you see billing impact."

Decisions made (short)
- Don't page SRE for single-consumer restart if lag auto-returns within 30m and backfill kicks off.
- Always notify customer with succinct root-cause + ETA for UI backfill.

Outstanding questions
- Do we have a rate-limited backfill mechanism to avoid saturating metrics-db when many tenants backfill at once? (ask infra-db team)
- Should the dashboard cache include user-override parameters (timezone, group_by) — risk vs. perf tradeoff.

End-of-run checklist (before closing this note)
- [ ] Create ENG-td ticket for restart guard + backfill automation (Maya)
- [ ] Push small UI bypass toggle (Luca)
- [ ] Draft customer note for Acme + Parcelly (Noah/Aisha)
- [ ] Add noise threshold for "metric decode failed" alert (me)

Quick timestamped micro-log: 
- 2026-03-09T02:34Z metrics-ingest-prod-3 restarted (kube event: OOMKill?) -> need to check kube events; file ticket if OOM.
- 2026-03-09T03:05Z manual restart -> backfill started (logs show reprocess start).

Personal: keep this short and actionable. When converting to a formal ticket, pull the relevant log excerpts and paste into JIRA as evidence.

---
Revision history:
- 2026-03-10: added outcome of restart and drafted customer note.
- 2026-02-25: initial scratchpad and morning plan.
